title: Scope the dev-link secure_path drop-in to the linking user
head: d696dd7b07d5
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A denied owner lookup silently completes the security migration
leads.consequence: After a successful read of a generated global rule, if the later sudo stat is denied or its credential expires, '|| true' makes owner empty and the migration exits 0. bin/omarchy-migrate:93-95 writes the per-user completion marker; the machine-wide rule remains indefinitely unless manually relinked or the marker removed. Distinguish failed privileged lookup from a genuinely missing checkout and retry on the former.

leads.summary: The control probe does not establish that a denied file probe meant absence
leads.consequence: When sudo test -f is denied or fails inspecting an existing rule but the independently authorized test -d / succeeds, the migration exits 0 without reading the rule. The migration runner records completion, leaving the global secure_path rule active. The control probe proves only that sudo could run another command, not that -f inspected the target. This path predates the latest commit but remains at the reviewed head.

leads.summary: Inherited fixture-path override can retire migration without inspecting the real rule
leads.consequence: An exported OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE naming an absent scratch path is inherited by omarchy-migrate's child. The sudo probes confirm that scratch path is absent, exit 0, and mark this migration complete while /etc/sudoers.d/omarchy-dev-path is still global. Restrict this test override to direct tests or clear it in the production runner. Open PR #10022 proposes clearing inherited OMARCHY_* variables, and would mitigate this issue if merged first.
leads.triage: Opus assessed: honored only in migration, same seam pattern as other migrations, requires caller to set it; not published

leads.summary: Migration silently skips a legacy rule generated for a checkout with double quotes in its path
leads.consequence: The legacy dev-link escaped a quote with a backslash inside the double-quoted secure_path, then visudo-validated and installed the global rule. The new regex uses [^"]* for the checkout and rejects that valid generated legacy output. It exits 0 without warning, so the migration is marked done while the global rule remains. Decode and validate the generator's actual escaping, or explicitly warn and keep this migration pending for affected paths.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus optional note 2; not published (budget, low value)

leads.summary: A root-owned checkout can still supply a writable bin, but is left globally trusted
leads.consequence: Owner of the checkout root alone says nothing about the checkout/bin directory, its symlink target, or files beneath it. A root-owned checkout with a group- or world-writable bin, or bin symlink to a user-writable tree, remains at the start of every sudoer's secure_path because this branch exits 0. Either verify the entire effective command path is non-writable by untrusted accounts or preserve the scoped migration/require explicit repair; never claim root ownership alone removes the risk.
leads.triage: pre-existing design since d003264b, outside follow-up delta, unverified; dropped

leads.summary: Migration test never proves that a generated legacy rule is migrated, and can pass on wrong-branch failures
leads.consequence: All three cases exercise errors or missing files, none tests a successful rewrite from Defaults to Defaults:<owner>. A migration that returns 0 for every existing readable rule but retains the two denial branches satisfies these assertions. The supposedly absent case (line 59) also omits the scratch-path override and the sudo stub delegates test/cat against /etc/sudoers.d/omarchy-dev-path (line 34): on a dev-linked test machine it may fail or test the wrong state; the first case also passes this literal path but its broken-sudo stub stops before touching it. In the final case, if the migration ignores the override and tests an absent path, the SUDO_FAIL_AFTER=1 stub rejects the second sudo call, producing the same 'Leaving this migration pending' line accepted by the test; no count or exact error branch is asserted. Point every case at a private drop-in path, add a successful rewrite fixture with stubbed stat/visudo/install and assert the exact scoped rule; for the denial case assert the read was reached (call trace), and compare the entire unchanged drop-in.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus test-validity notes; published as two optional test notes in Details

leads.summary: Open PRs #8466 and #13047 overlap exact changed lines and require joint conflict resolution
leads.consequence: Read-only git merge-file using each other PR's own base/head produced conflict markers at both locations. #8466's status branch would restore the misleading 'sudo resolves omarchy-*' wording if selected over this PR's 'commands' line, while its session-state case must also survive; #13047's factory-reset exception should be retained alongside the secure_path documentation. GitHub currently reports each other PR MERGEABLE against its own base, not against this head. Their files cannot be combined as-is; resolve both hunks explicitly in the second merge.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator with git merge-file on fetched blobs (triage/) and by Opus; published as one Details line

limits: The controlled run used stubbed sudo/stat/install/visudo with a read-only PR source snapshot and LC_ALL=C; it does not claim live sudo/PAM/account behavior or test the full repository suite.
The sudo source inspected was v1.9.17p2 upstream; the exact sudo version distributed on the target Omarchy release was not pinned in this hunt.
Do not infer any future merge outcome: #10022, #8466 and #13047 are currently separate open PRs.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `d696dd7b`, two sudo steps can still retire the migration, and accounts without sudo cannot finish it.

Both [earlier findings](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12883#issuecomment-5792115649) are resolved as cited.

### Two sudo steps can still retire the migration

`sudo stat ... || true` (line 59) reads a failed sudo as an empty owner, and the probe (lines 19-22) exits 0 when only the first `sudo test` fails. **Impact:** in these uncommon cases, it is marked applied while the global rule stays.

**Suggested change:** Do each privileged check in one sudo call that reports its state and fails when sudo fails.

<details><summary>Reproducer: owner lookup (fails at d696dd7b)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/dev-link-migration-owner-lookup-test.sh` in the PR checkout and run `bash test/shell.d/dev-link-migration-owner-lookup-test.sh`. It uses a sudo test double (never real sudo) and the PR's `OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE` override. The first case is a control (sudo working, rule gets scoped). The second makes only sudo call 3 (`stat`) fail, after `test -f` (call 1) and `cat` (call 2) succeeded.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1790064412.sh"
test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_dir/bin"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"

# The sudo double from dev-link-migration-test.sh, generalised: SUDO_FAIL_CALLS
# lists the call numbers that fail the way a denied or unanswered sudo does.
# `install` copies the staged file instead of changing ownership.
cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
count=$(( $(< "$SUDO_CALL_COUNT") + 1 ))
printf '%s' "$count" >"$SUDO_CALL_COUNT"
for n in ${SUDO_FAIL_CALLS:-}; do
  if (( n == count )); then
    echo "sudo: a password is required" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
if [[ $1 == install ]]; then
  cp "${@: -2:1}" "${@: -1}"
  exit
fi
exec "$@"
STUB
chmod +x "$stub_bin/sudo"

checkout="$test_dir/checkout"
mkdir -p "$checkout/bin"
drop_in="$test_dir/omarchy-dev-path"
legacy="Defaults secure_path=\"$checkout/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin\""

run_migration() {
  printf '%s\n' "$legacy" >"$drop_in"
  printf '0' >"$test_dir/calls"
  migration_status=0
  migration_output=$(env PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" SUDO_CALL_COUNT="$test_dir/calls" \
    OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE="$drop_in" "$@" bash -euo pipefail "$migration" 2>&1) ||
    migration_status=$?
  migration_output=${migration_output//$test_dir/\$test_dir}
}

# Control: with sudo working, the legacy rule is scoped to the checkout owner.
run_migration
[[ $(<"$drop_in") == "Defaults:$(stat -c %U "$checkout") "* ]] ||
  fail "migration scopes the legacy rule when sudo works" "exit $migration_status: $migration_output"
pass "migration scopes the legacy rule when sudo works"

# sudo serves `test -f` (call 1) and `cat` (call 2), then fails at `stat` (call 3).
# The migration must not retire while the global rule is still in place.
run_migration SUDO_FAIL_CALLS=3
if (( migration_status == 0 )) && [[ $(<"$drop_in") == "$legacy" ]]; then
  fail "a sudo failure at the owner lookup leaves the migration pending" \
    "exit $migration_status, drop-in unchanged, output: $migration_output"
fi
pass "a sudo failure at the owner lookup leaves the migration pending"
```

Actual output at d696dd7b (exit status 1):

```text
ok - migration scopes the legacy rule when sudo works
exit 0, drop-in unchanged, output: Scope the dev-link sudoers drop-in to the linking user
Left $test_dir/omarchy-dev-path alone: cannot tell which user $test_dir/checkout belongs to.
Re-run 'omarchy dev link $test_dir/checkout' as that user, or 'omarchy dev unlink'.
not ok - a sudo failure at the owner lookup leaves the migration pending
```

With the owner lookup done in one elevated call that fails when sudo fails (for example `sudo bash -c 'if [[ -e $1 ]]; then stat -c %U -- "$1"; fi' bash "$checkout"`, checked with `if ! owner=$(...)`), both cases print `ok` and the PR's own `dev-link-migration-test.sh` still passes (checked on a disposable copy of the migration).
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: probe retry (fails at d696dd7b)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/dev-link-migration-probe-retry-test.sh` in the PR checkout and run `bash test/shell.d/dev-link-migration-probe-retry-test.sh`. It uses a sudo test double (never real sudo) and the PR's `OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE` override. Only sudo call 1 fails.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1790064412.sh"
test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_dir/bin"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"

# SUDO_FAIL_CALLS lists the call numbers that fail the way a password prompt
# that timed out does; every other call runs. `install` copies instead of chown.
cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
count=$(( $(< "$SUDO_CALL_COUNT") + 1 ))
printf '%s' "$count" >"$SUDO_CALL_COUNT"
for n in ${SUDO_FAIL_CALLS:-}; do
  if (( n == count )); then
    echo "sudo: timed out reading password" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
if [[ $1 == install ]]; then
  cp "${@: -2:1}" "${@: -1}"
  exit
fi
exec "$@"
STUB
chmod +x "$stub_bin/sudo"

checkout="$test_dir/checkout"
mkdir -p "$checkout/bin"
drop_in="$test_dir/omarchy-dev-path"
legacy="Defaults secure_path=\"$checkout/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin\""
printf '%s\n' "$legacy" >"$drop_in"
printf '0' >"$test_dir/calls"

# The first prompt (`sudo test -f`) fails, the second (`sudo test -d /`) succeeds:
# an unattended update whose first prompt timed out, answered on return.
migration_status=0
migration_output=$(env PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" SUDO_CALL_COUNT="$test_dir/calls" SUDO_FAIL_CALLS=1 \
  OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE="$drop_in" bash -euo pipefail "$migration" 2>&1) ||
  migration_status=$?
migration_output=${migration_output//$test_dir/\$test_dir}

if (( migration_status == 0 )) && [[ $(<"$drop_in") == "$legacy" ]]; then
  fail "a failed first sudo prompt does not retire the migration with the global rule in place" \
    "exit $migration_status, drop-in unchanged, sudo calls: $(<"$test_dir/calls"), output: $migration_output"
fi
pass "a failed first sudo prompt does not retire the migration with the global rule in place"
```

Actual output at d696dd7b (exit status 1):

```text
exit 0, drop-in unchanged, sudo calls: 2, output: Scope the dev-link sudoers drop-in to the linking user
sudo: timed out reading password
not ok - a failed first sudo prompt does not retire the migration with the global rule in place
```

With the probe done in one elevated call that prints the state (for example `kind=$(sudo bash -c 'if [[ -f $1 ]]; then printf file; elif [[ -e $1 ]]; then printf other; else printf missing; fi' bash "$sudoers_file")`, checked with `if !`, the pattern `inspect_sudoers_file` in `migrations/1788025225.sh` uses), this test prints `ok` and the PR's own tests still pass (checked on a disposable copy of the migration).
</details>

### Accounts without sudo get stuck

The probe needs sudo even with no drop-in, and since `6f4d760b` its failure exits 1. **Impact:** an account without sudo fails every run, halting its queue.

**Suggested change:** After a successful privileged pass, write a root-owned machine marker and exit 0 early when it exists.

<details><summary>Reproducer: account without sudo (at d696dd7b)</summary>

Save as `non-sudo-account-queue.sh` in the root of the PR checkout and run `bash non-sudo-account-queue.sh`. It uses a sudo double that always refuses, a temporary `OMARCHY_PATH` and migration state directory, and the PR's `OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE` override pointed at a path that does not exist.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Demonstration, not a pass/fail test: an account that cannot use sudo runs
# omarchy-migrate on a machine that has no dev-link drop-in at all.
# Run from the PR checkout root: bash non-sudo-account-queue.sh

set -uo pipefail

root=$(pwd)
test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$test_dir/bin" "$test_dir/home" "$test_dir/state" "$test_dir/omarchy/migrations"

cat >"$test_dir/bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
echo "sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file" >&2
exit 1
STUB
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$test_dir/bin/omarchy-notification-dismiss"
chmod +x "$test_dir/bin"/*

cp "$root/migrations/1790064412.sh" "$test_dir/omarchy/migrations/"
printf 'echo "Later migration"\ntouch "$HOME/later-migration-ran"\n' >"$test_dir/omarchy/migrations/1799999999.sh"

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  env PATH="$test_dir/bin:$PATH" HOME="$test_dir/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$test_dir/omarchy" \
    OMARCHY_MIGRATION_STATE="$test_dir/state" OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE="$test_dir/no-such-drop-in" \
    bash "$root/bin/omarchy-migrate" >"$test_dir/out" 2>&1
  status=$?
  sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' -e "s|$test_dir|\$test_dir|g" "$test_dir/out" | grep -v '^$'
  echo "attempt $attempt: omarchy-migrate exit $status;" \
    "completed: $(ls "$test_dir/state" | tr '\n' ' ')" \
    "later migration ran: $([[ -e $test_dir/home/later-migration-ran ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
done
```

Actual output at d696dd7b:

```text
Running migration (1790064412)
Scope the dev-link sudoers drop-in to the linking user
sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file
sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file
Could not inspect $test_dir/no-such-drop-in. Leaving this migration pending so it retries.
attempt 1: omarchy-migrate exit 1; completed:  later migration ran: no
Running migration (1790064412)
Scope the dev-link sudoers drop-in to the linking user
sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file
sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file
Could not inspect $test_dir/no-such-drop-in. Leaving this migration pending so it retries.
attempt 2: omarchy-migrate exit 1; completed:  later migration ran: no
Running migration (1790064412)
Scope the dev-link sudoers drop-in to the linking user
sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file
sudo: this account is not in the sudoers file
Could not inspect $test_dir/no-such-drop-in. Leaving this migration pending so it retries.
attempt 3: omarchy-migrate exit 1; completed:  later migration ran: no
```

Control (same setup, sudo double that works): the runner exits 0, both markers are written and the later migration runs.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Note:** The owner lookup has been in the migration since `d003264b`; earlier reviews did not name it. Both remaining paths need sudo to fail after earlier calls succeeded (for example a command-specific policy), or a failed first prompt followed by an answered one. The non-sudo exit 1 came in with `6f4d760b`, which followed the first review's suggestion to propagate sudo errors. `migrations/1788025225.sh` has both patterns: one-call `inspect_sudoers_file` and a machine marker under `/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/` that accounts without sudo can read; those accounts stay blocked until an administrator has run the migration once.

**Verified:**
- A sudo failure at the read exits 1 with the drop-in unchanged. The same failure exited 0 in the `6f4d760b` migration once it was pointed at the same drop-in.
- Persistent sudo failure at the probe exits 1; an absent drop-in with working sudo is still a clean no-op.
- Reading with `sudo cat` and filtering locally gave the same result as the previous `sudo grep` in 15 content cases, including empty, comment-only, CRLF and no final newline.
- The PR's link, unlink and migration tests pass.

**Optional test improvement:** The new read-failure case also passes against the `6f4d760b` migration, which ignores the override and fails at the probe instead; both failure messages contain "Leaving this migration pending". Asserting `Could not read` would pin it to the read.

**Optional test improvement:** The first two migration cases still use the real `/etc/sudoers.d/omarchy-dev-path`, so the absent-file case passes because an unprivileged test cannot see that file. Pointing them at `$test_dir` through `OMARCHY_DEV_SUDOERS_FILE` would make them hermetic.

**Related open PRs:** a three-way merge of the files conflicts with #8466 in `bin/omarchy-dev-status` (its status line still says `omarchy-*`) and with #13047 in `docs/file-layout.md` (its factory-reset paragraph).
</details>
